newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes firmer at day's high in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes firmer at day's high in Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed firmer at the day's high on Wednesday as late bargain-hunting and shortcovering offset early selling after a day of two-way trading, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$338.20/70 an ounce, up from New York's $337.50/348.00 close on Tuesday.

"The market players were shortcovering, believing that gold had seen its lowest point and was recovering," said a dealer at a local investment house. "But the direction remained confused, with sentiment still leaning towards bearishness."
Dealers said gold would now range-trade between $337 and $341.
Local gold ended HK$7 lower at HK$3,133 a tael.
